models.name: c2f_byte
models.title: C2F-byte (concept)
models.description: Byte encoder, fixed patches of P bytes, E1-style global stack on patches with a one-patch causal shift, expansion back to byte positions, a shared-weight byte refinement loop x r, and a 256-way byte head.

cost_model.formula: mflops_per_bpe_token_equivalent(P, r) = global_term / P + local_base + per_pass * (r - 1)
cost_model.global_term_derivation: E1 body = 91.03 - 18.9 head = 72.13 MFLOPs per token; one patch is costed like one E1 token; one BPE token = 3.735 bytes, so 72.13 * 3.735 = 269.4
cost_model.local_base_derivation: note table, P=4, r=1: 95 M total, minus 269.4 / 4 = 67.35 M global
cost_model.per_pass_derivation: note: each extra refinement pass costs about 13 M (d_local = 192)
cost_model.extrapolation_warning: Only the P = 4 row (95 / 108 / 135 M, 1.04 / 1.19 / 1.48 x E1) is in the note. P = 2 and P = 8 are our 1/P extrapolation of the global term, not a measurement and not in the note.

estimate_notes: Design concept: nothing here has been trained. FLOP figures are estimates (6 x active params per position; attention-score terms ignored).
Global stack = E1's six blocks (swa, gdn, gdn, swa, gdn, attn) run on patch positions, not on bytes.
Byte-level blocks (encoder and refinement) are E1's gdn and swa blocks scaled by (192/384)^2 = 0.25 for parameters; their size here is illustrative, not a parameter count from the byte model.
The byte-level SWA window of 64 bytes is a drawing assumption (the note only says 'small-window').
Parameter totals are not estimated here. See notes/byte-quest.md when the byte model lands.
Literature prior: byte models trail BPE below about 4B parameters on code, so the arc's claims are about granularity and loops, not beating BPE-E1.
